title: Update the api key, after the initialization.
body: We've had a user [asking how it was possible to change the API key after the initialization](https://discourse.algolia.com/t/is-there-a-way-to-switch-between-two-keys/2788) of instantsearch.js. Right now, it's not possible and I'm creating this issue in order to follow up on that issue.

comments.body: If we're creating an API to change the keys after initialisation, we should also think about allowing to change other parameters in a similar way, WDYT?
True. However there is a difference because the API key can't even be changed at the helper level. And what about the js client level?
I think that in v4 you should be able to pass it as a requestOption, but I'd have to test if it's actually possible.

Now that we have a `searchClient` that can be passed to the paremeters, we could have a setSearchClient to update the client? (since that's the client that holds the credentials on Algolia, maybe that could be a good solution?). cc @algolia/instantsearch-for-websites
Are you proposing that we have a setSearchClient to solve the original issue about update the API Key?
Seems possible, but not sure if that's the best API we can find
A `setSearchClient()` method could also allow to change the endpoint depending on external events, it'd be quite powerful.

> Are you proposing that we have a setSearchClient to solve the original issue about update the API Key?

Yes



> Seems possible, but not sure if that's the best API we can find

Yes that's not the most friendly. I think that maybe we need to sync about completely decoupling InstantSearch.js from the client. I'm not sure we're on the same page as a team :)
I agree about that, but it just seems odd to only allow updating of a search client, and none of the other parameters of `instantsearch()`, I'd rather have a fluid API for all of those use cases

> I agree about that, but it just seems odd to only allow updating of a search client, and none of the other parameters of instantsearch(), I'd rather have a fluid API for all of those use cases

It's a work in progress :) We've added the means to update the widgets. @Haroenv 

Can you tell us more about a fluid API? Do you have something in mind already? :)

Right now you can do that by setting `instantSearchInstance.searchClient = newSearchClient`, this is not documented and supported, but will work.

We can rediscuss at a later point a good API to update parameters of all widgets, including the root, this doesn't seem like the correct issue to do that
